rows.text: The Gemma B70 decode benchmark evaluates autoregressive throughput under varying KV cache constraints. To establish a reliable benchmark, the test utilizes a fixed prompt length to isolate decoding latency. This benchmark measures tokens per second (TPS) across multiple GPU configurations. A critical benchmark metric is the memory bandwidth utilization during the decoding phase. In this benchmark, the B70 architecture demonstrates high efficiency in compute-bound scenarios. However, the benchmark reveals significant bottlenecks when the batch size increases, shifting the benchmark focus toward memory-bound limitations. Every benchmark iteration maintains a consistent temperature setting to ensure benchmark reproducibility. The benchmark results indicate that quantization significantly impacts the benchmark performance scores. Consequently, the benchmark serves as a primary tool for optimizing the Gemma B70 inference pipeline. Final benchmark analysis suggests that scaling the benchmark to larger context windows requires advanced attention mechanisms to maintain benchmark stability.
